scene.note: rota.js calls the plots to the tap on a timer, and stops cleanly when Rhiannon types stop or presses Ctrl+C, saying who goes first next time.

steps.note: rota.js reads the plots in their order, and the length of a turn typed after its name.
The first plot is called at once, and the timer calls the next one each time a turn is over.
After the last turn, it says everyone has had one, stops the timer, and the script ends by itself.
The turns are being called when it starts to rain.
Rhiannon types stop. Other lines typed change nothing.
rota.js says who would have been next, stops the timer and stops reading what is typed, so the script ends.
This time Rhiannon presses Ctrl+C, which sends the script a signal.
A listener for the signal runs instead of the script stopping on the spot.
It tidies up exactly as a typed stop does, and says who goes first next time.
